```{python}
#| label: fig-length-scales
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Length scales of integrated-circuit structures compared to familiar objects, on a logarithmic axis."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

items = [
    ('Si lattice spacing', 0.24e-9),
    ('SiO$_2$ gate oxide', 2e-9),
    ('Leading-edge feature size', 15e-9),
    ('MOSFET gate (130 nm node)', 130e-9),
    ('Virus', 150e-9),
    ('Visible light wavelength', 550e-9),
    ('Red blood cell', 8e-6),
    ('Human hair', 70e-6),
    ('This letter "m"', 2e-3),
]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.2))
y = np.arange(len(items))
sizes = [s for _, s in items]
ax.hlines(y, 1e-10, sizes, color='lightgray', lw=1)
ax.plot(sizes, y, 'o', color='tab:blue')
for yi, (name, s) in zip(y, items):
    ax.text(s * 1.6, yi, name, va='center', fontsize=9)

ax.set_xscale('log')
ax.set_xlim(1e-10, 3e-1)
ax.set_ylim(-0.7, len(items) - 0.3)
ax.set_xlabel('Size (m)')
ax.set_yticks([])
ax.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)
for spine in ['left', 'right', 'top']:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
